[0] At last night's Emmy Awards ceremony, Apple TV+ put on an impressive showing, beating out competitors including HBO to become the most-awarded platform of the night. Below is HBO's Casey Bloys' response to Apple TV+'s wins.

[1] [1] The HBO CEO praised Apple TV+'s impressive performance while also acknowledging that competing with a trillion-dollar company is "quite a challenge."

[2] [2] Apple TV+ has long been compared to HBO, as both prioritize quality over quantity. Apple has even occasionally been dubbed the "new HBO."

[3] [3] Last night's Emmys further cemented that notion, with Apple TV+ surpassing HBO, Netflix, and other platforms to claim the top spot as the most-awarded platform of the night.

[4] [4] Apple TV+ swept a total of 29 awards, earning the honour of "most-awarded network of the year," with shows like *Widow's Bay* putting in particularly strong performances. HBO followed closely behind with 21 awards.

[5] [5] Following the Emmy Awards ceremony, HBO executive Casey Bloys sat down for an interview with Deadline and was asked for his thoughts on Apple TV+'s performance. His response is as follows:

[6] [6] DEADLINE: What are your thoughts on Apple TV+'s performance this time around? They became the most-awarded platform at the Emmys for the first time—is there anything you'd like to say? BLOYS: To be honest, I'm actually quite thrilled, because I think they're strong competitors—Zack and Jamie. We've always had strong rivals—Showtime, FX, AMC, Netflix, Amazon—so Apple joining the fray has everyone on their toes, and this is exactly when I perform at my best. They're a trillion-dollar company, so there's no question it's a big challenge, but we're going to keep doing what we've always been doing—producing the best shows out there.

[7] [7] Bloys joined HBO in 2004 and has been overseeing programming since 2016. His track record speaks for itself, and his response to Apple TV+'s wins was largely gracious and sincere, offering heartfelt congratulations.

[8] [8] However, the most interesting part of his response was this line: "They're a trillion-dollar company, so there's no question it's a big challenge."

[9] [9] We don't know Apple TV+'s internal budget, but there's no denying that Apple's overall financial resources far surpass those of most competitors, including HBO.

[10] [10] Coincidentally, Paramount is currently actively seeking to acquire HBO (along with other Warner Bros. Discovery assets), hoping to compete more effectively with tech giants like Apple and Amazon.

[11] [11] Does scale naturally bring advantages? Perhaps. But plenty of networks have already proven that, when it comes to producing content audiences love, money is only a small part of the equation.

[12] [12] Apple TV+ costs $14.99 per month, or can be purchased as part of the Apple One subscription bundle.
